bullets.title: NVIDIA Vera Rubin launch: 10x throughput vs. Blackwell, CPO in volume manufacturing
bullets.body: NVIDIA launched the Vera Rubin NVL72 rack-scale supercomputer on July 21, delivering 10x higher tokens/megawatt vs. Grace Blackwell NVL72 (800K vs. 80K tokens/s at same 150MW draw). Crucially, NVIDIA confirmed its co-packaged optics (CPO) switch for scale-out networking is now in 'volume manufacturing,' resolving prior concerns. Wistron opened a $700M, 324K sq-ft Texas facility already producing GB300 Grace Blackwell Ultra systems and preparing a cell for Vera Rubin.

bullets.title: NVDA Vera Rubin supply: 1,000 racks/day capacity, ~$630B annualized; DRAM cut in half
bullets.body: Per The Information (via GavinSBaker), NVIDIA can manufacture ~1,000 Vera Rubin racks per day, implying ~$630B in annualized production capacity. SemiAnalysis reports NVIDIA cut DRAM on Vera Rubin by 50%, betting on CMX/flash offload to reduce inference memory requirements—a potential headwind for DRAM suppliers.

bullets.title: GPU supply tightening post-Kimi K3: B200 at 0%, GH200 rapidly tightening
bullets.body: Multiple fintwit accounts (WarrenPies/SemiAnalysis retweeted) note GPU availability is tightening again: B200 already sold out at 0% availability, GH200 tightening aggressively following Kimi K3 launch. Reads as broadly bullish for NVDA near-term demand.

bullets.title: SMCI: $60B+ record Q4 backlog, but Q4 revenue near low end of $11B-$12.5B guide
bullets.body: Super Micro disclosed a record backlog from over $60B in new Q4 FY2026 orders. However, Q4 revenue is expected near the low end of the $11B–$12.5B guidance range. On the positive side, Q4 gross margin guidance raised to 15–17% on favorable customer/product mix. Stock +15% after-hours.

bullets.title: META custom AMD MI400-series chip: half MI455X size, optimized for recsys, LLM-suboptimal
bullets.body: SemiAnalysis/SemiDoped breaks: Meta is developing a custom AMD MI400-series chip roughly half the physical size of a standard MI455X, using 144GB HBM vs. 432GB standard, specifically optimized for recommendation systems. The chip is poorly suited for LLM training/inference, and Meta's custom packaging will complicate rental strategies. Critics flag this as emblematic of Meta's infrastructure over-engineering.

bullets.title: Intel Ohio fab: denies outright sale; SK Hynix denies acquisition; JV possibility unaddressed
bullets.body: Intel formally denied selling its Ohio fab; SK Hynix denied plans to acquire it. However, neither party addressed a potential joint venture structure, which multiple observers (including chip analyst @jukan05/SemiAnalysis) view as the most likely outcome. SK Hynix proximity to Purdue/Ohio State engineering talent cited as strategic rationale.

bullets.title: Taiwan June export orders hit record $95.26B (+59.4% YoY), electronics +79.9%
bullets.body: Taiwan's June export orders surged 59.4% YoY to a record $95.26B, blowing past 47.3% expectations. Electronics orders rose 79.9% to $40.5B and IT/communications +81.9% to $34.15B, with US orders leading at +83.6%. Strong positive read-through for the semiconductor supply chain including TSM.

bullets.title: TSMC to raise chipmaking prices by up to 10% from 2027
bullets.body: Nikkei Asia reports TSMC plans to raise chipmaking prices by up to 10% starting in 2027. This would be a meaningful pricing power signal and a margin tailwind for TSM, while adding to cost pressures for chip designers.

bullets.title: VAT Group Q2 record orders (CHF500m) — leading indicator for AMAT, LRCX
bullets.body: VAT Group reported a record Q2 order intake of CHF500m, led by semiconductor valves, with backlog reaching CHF648m. The author notes VAT's order book is a leading indicator for tool OEMs, implying a positive forward read-through for AMAT and LRCX.

bullets.title: MU: $40M put sale to open signals bullish positioning; short-seller thesis challenged
bullets.body: Unusual Whales flagged $40M in MU puts sold to open — an unusually large premium-collection/bullish bet. Separately, a fintwit account dismissed MU short sellers as 'brain dead and crazy risk-takers' with no fundamental basis. MU listed among top S&P 500 gainers today (+10%+).

bullets.title: Open-source AI and HBM demand: BofA's Arya questions demand concentration
bullets.body: BofA's Vivek Arya (via fintwit) raised the question of whether open-source AI distributes HBM demand (each deployment creates its own memory footprint) vs. closed models which concentrate HBM demand in shared hyperscaler pools. The framing is relevant for MU/SNDK demand sustainability.

bullets.title: Photonics bottleneck shifting: CPO volume manufacturing validates LITE, AAOI thesis
bullets.body: Multiple accounts flag that NVIDIA's confirmation of CPO switch in 'volume manufacturing' is hyper-bullish for co-packaged optics names. One author tracking CW lasers notes supply-demand gap continues to widen with massive new CW supply expected in 2027-2028 across multiple companies. FN ($19B mkt cap) flagged as undercovered with $1.27B next-quarter guide (+39.6% YoY).

bullets.title: Apple P/E at 40x vs. 26x 10-year avg; elevated multiples flagged ahead of earnings
bullets.body: Charliebilello data (via fintwit): AAPL P/E is 40x vs. 10-year average of 26x; EV/EBITDA at 31x vs. 19x 10-year average. Elevated multiples flagged as a concern heading into big tech earnings week.

bullets.title: S&P 500 price-breadth divergence matches entire dot-com bubble; concentration at 50-year high
bullets.body: S&P 500 price and breadth have moved in opposite directions on 52 trading days YTD — equaling the full 2000 dot-com peak total. Separately, the 24 largest stocks now account for >50% of S&P 500 market cap, the highest concentration in history. Semiconductors now represent 14% of total market cap, nearly double the dot-com peak.

bullets.title: Macro: NQ futures -0.9% pre-market; AI stock rally losing steam ahead of Mag-7 earnings
bullets.body: Nasdaq 100 futures are down 0.9% and S&P e-mini futures down 0.4% as of pre-market. Headlines note the AI stock rally is losing momentum ahead of key Magnificent Seven earnings (GOOGL, TSLA, MSFT among those reporting). Bearish positioning near record highs.

bullets.title: Geopolitical risk: Strait of Hormuz effectively closed; Brent above $91/bbl
bullets.body: Iran has attacked 30+ commercial vessels over three months; CENTCOM reports 11 consecutive nights of U.S. strikes on Iranian military targets. Brent crude settled at $91.01 (+2.01%); one account flagged Brent touching $95 with Hormuz transits at zero. Japan Finance Minister calls the situation 'very difficult.' Yen at 39-year low of ¥163/USD.

bullets.title: GOOGL: Australia ACCC proposes authorizing Google Play Store fees through 2032
bullets.body: Australia's competition regulator proposes a draft determination authorizing Google and Epic Games' settlement terms through September 30, 2032, governing Google Play service fees for developers. Limits regulatory uncertainty for GOOGL's app store monetization in Australia.

bullets.title: TSLA: FSD 14.3.6 released; Cybercab on display at Tesla Diner; L3 adoption debate
bullets.body: Tesla released FSD version 14.3.6. The Cybercab was placed on public display at the Tesla Diner. Separately, fintwit discusses L3 autonomous vehicle approval requiring 99.99%+ reliability, with one investor asserting Tesla will be first and best to market. Long-horizon self-driving debate (7-15 years to widespread adoption) continues.

bullets.title: NVDA RTX Spark AI PC platform debuting Fall; Wistron Texas manufacturing underway
bullets.body: NVIDIA's RTX Spark chip platform for AI PCs launches this Fall, with Asustek and MSI as first Taiwan OEM adopters. Jensen Huang attended opening of Wistron's Fort Worth facility (324K sq ft, $700M) already producing GB300 Grace Blackwell compute boards, with a separate manufacturing cell being prepared for Vera Rubin Superchip.

bullets.title: White House redirects $200B federal research budget toward AI; tariff escalation on track
bullets.body: The White House plans to redirect ~$200B in annual federal research funding toward AI and individual scientists, away from traditional university grants. Separately, Trump's temporary 10% global tariff expires Friday with new country-specific tariffs expected 'as early as this week,' and 100% tariffs on imported generic drugs announced for August 2028 (escalating to 200%).
